To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the magnitude of lifestyle factors in predicting fatness varies across ethnic groups, and that the strongest associations with lifestyle factors were found for total fat mass.
lifestyle behaviours were associated with adiposity in youth of multiple ethnic groups from 4 countries, with the strongest relationships observed between lifestyle and TFM.
lifestyle risk factors for overweight and obesity are associated with adiposity and that the magnitude of the association varies by lifestyle factor.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the size of the relationship between obesity-related risk factors and fatness.
the relationship between lifestyle behaviours and adiposity in a heterogeneous sample of youth from 4 countries of the Pacific.
the association between lifestyle risk factors and adiposity in a large heterogeneous sample of young people.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
lifestyle risk factors are associated with a 2.5 to 3.6 % increase in fatness for every 1 unit increase in the risk factor, and that these relationships are stronger for TFM than for BMI.
lifestyle behaviours are strongly and dose-dependently related to fatness.
lifestyle behaviours are associated with fatness in a sizeable, but not overwhelming, dose-dependent manner.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
lifestyle factors have a small to moderate effect on fatness.
TV watching, soft drink consumption and breakfast consumption are important contributors to obesity aetiology, but after-school physical activity is less important.
TV watching, soft drink consumption, breakfast consumption and after-school physical are important risk factors for obesity in youth, and should be targeted for prevention and treatment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the lifestyle risk factors for childhood obesity are associated with meaningful changes in body composition.
lifestyle factors, particularly TV watching, are strongly related to fatness and that the size of these relationships is similar across ethnic groups.
lifestyle behaviours are strongly related to adiposity in a dose-dependent way and that this association is strongest for TFM.
